action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 IgG positive only at low titer (1:10), to be read with the CSF; metabolic, thyroid, neuronal-surface, onconeural, HIV, beta-hCG and toxicology results normal
action_criteria.label: Obtain the serum work-up: blood count, chemistry, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV, beta-hCG and a cell-based serum anti-GluN1 IgG assay read together with the CSF result
action_criteria.rationale: Screens metabolic, endocrine, toxic, infectious and pregnancy-related causes of acute psychosis, and pairs the low-titer serum antibody with the decisive CSF assay.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Essentially normal MRI: two punctate nonspecific right frontal white matter foci, normal medial temporal lobes, no enhancement
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP; it is normal in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal cell count (3 cells/uL), borderline IgG index and equivocal oligoclonal bands; HSV-1/2 PCR negative; CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:32)
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, oligoclonal bands or IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay
action_criteria.rationale: With only two symptom groups the probable criteria are not met even with the teratoma (which lowers the threshold to three groups), so the CSF anti-GluN1 cell-based assay is what establishes the diagnosis; HSV PCR addresses the infectious mimic.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mild diffuse slowing with frontal intermittent rhythmic delta; no epileptiform discharges or extreme delta brush; staring episodes without clear electrographic correlate
action_criteria.label: Obtain an EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, including extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: An abnormal EEG is a Graus 2016 supporting finding in a patient with normal CSF cells and MRI, and the staring episodes need electrographic characterization.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: 1.6 cm left ovarian complex cystic lesion with an echogenic shadowing mural nodule: mature cystic teratoma
action_criteria.label: Screen for an ovarian teratoma with pelvic and abdominal ultrasound
action_criteria.rationale: Women of reproductive age carry the highest teratoma risk; tumor removal is part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG to quantify seizure burden while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist
action_criteria.rationale: Recurrent staring episodes with behavioral arrest were not captured electrographically on a 30-minute record, so a prolonged recording is needed to detect non-convulsive seizures.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Estrogen-containing contraceptive with IVIG thrombosis risk; sertraline and sodium monitoring
action_criteria.label: Check the patient's medications against the drugs the acute plan needs (acyclovir, corticosteroids, IVIG, antiseizure medication)
action_criteria.rationale: No interaction here changes the first-line plan; the check confirms the contraceptive issue before IVIG.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1-2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Arrange prompt surgical removal of the left ovarian teratoma (laparoscopic, ovary-sparing where feasible) as part of first-line treatment, with gynecology.
Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam or lacosamide; avoid valproate in a woman able to become pregnant; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.
Admit to a neurology ward with seizure precautions and continuous cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation and insomnia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first; do not start the risperidone prescribed at urgent care.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioral management; gynecology for the teratoma.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.
DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis, whose movement disorders are antibody-mediated rather than presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.key_features: Afebrile; CSF acellular with HSV-1/2 PCR negative; normal medial temporal lobes on MRI; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B or AMPA receptor)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, DPPX) and onconeural antibodies negative; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

Staring episodes with behavioral arrest, fluctuating recognition, an abnormal EEG with FIRDA, a left frontotemporal seizure on continuous EEG and CSF anti-GluN1 antibodies are not explained by a primary psychosis or her anxiety disorder.
Mother has SLE, but ANA is only 1:40 with no rash, arthritis, cytopenia or raised ESR, and the CSF anti-GluN1 result accounts for the syndrome.
Urine drug screen negative and blood ethanol undetectable; risperidone never taken; stable sertraline 50 mg without clonus, hyperthermia or autonomic signs.

key_clinical_evidence: One week of subacute behavioral change (paranoia, insomnia, disorganization) with cognitive deficits after a viral-like prodrome, plus brief staring episodes with behavioral arrest: two of the six Graus 2016 groups (psychiatric/cognitive and probable seizures; speech is fluent, consciousness is preserved and there are no dyskinesias or autonomic signs). That is fewer than the three groups that would suffice with a teratoma, so the probable criteria are not met before the antibody result.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:32) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); the low-titer serum positive (1:10) is read with the CSF and would not be enough alone.

CSF has a normal cell count with only borderline IgG index and equivocal bands, and MRI is essentially normal; a normal MRI and CSF do not exclude the disease, and here they exclude HSV encephalitis and structural causes.

EEG shows mild diffuse slowing with FIRDA; continuous EEG captures a left frontotemporal electrographic seizure and delta-beta activity short of extreme delta brush, which supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
Pelvic ultrasound shows a 1.6 cm left ovarian mature cystic teratoma: its removal is part of first-line treatment.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumor removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Staring episodes, fluctuating recognition, cognitive deficits and an abnormal EEG alongside the psychiatric change mandate exclusion of anti-NMDAR encephalitis before a psychiatric diagnosis is accepted.
red_herrings.data_point: Acute psychiatric presentation (insomnia, paranoia, disorganized behavior) in a young woman with generalized anxiety disorder after a breakup and examinations, diagnosed at urgent care as an acute psychotic episode.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: CSF and MRI can be normal in anti-NMDAR encephalitis, especially early; the CSF anti-GluN1 cell-based assay decides the diagnosis.
red_herrings.data_point: Normal CSF cell count (3 cells/uL) with borderline IgG index and an essentially normal brain MRI.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests that an inflammatory encephalitis has been excluded.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses.
red_herrings.data_point: Mild cold with rhinorrhea and sore throat about ten days before presentation.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Points toward a viral encephalitis or a post-viral psychiatric reaction.

contraindications: Aspirin allergy (urticaria): none of the proposed drugs is aspirin or an NSAID.
Haloperidol and other high-potency D2 antagonists: class warning for severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions in suspected autoimmune encephalitis.
interactions: Ethinylestradiol (combined oral contraceptive) with IVIG: estrogen use is a listed risk factor for IVIG-associated thrombosis; ensure hydration and the slowest practical infusion rate.
Ethinylestradiol with methylprednisolone: estrogens reduce corticosteroid clearance; effect modest at pulse doses.
Sertraline: SSRIs can cause SIADH; monitor sodium during IVIG and fluid therapy. No clinically relevant interaction with acyclovir, methylprednisolone or levetiracetam.
Levetiracetam: no clinically relevant interaction with the current medicines; irritability and behavioral change are recognized adverse effects.
Acyclovir: no interaction with the current medicines; dose by renal function and maintain hydration.

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.query: anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titers related more closely to outcome than serum titers.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumor, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumor removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Extreme delta brush was found in 7 of 23 adults with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis and was associated with a more prolonged illness.
Severe intolerance to antipsychotics (rigidity, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions) was frequent in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis who received them.
results.source: Lejuste F et al. Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2016;3:e280

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumor removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

metadata.diagnostic_challenge_notes: This case is designed as a diagnostic puzzle where the initial presentation mimics a primary psychiatric disorder. Nearly all initial workup results (labs, MRI, CSF) are normal or near-normal, making the diagnosis extremely easy to miss. The key to solving this puzzle is recognizing the subtle red flags and having a high index of suspicion for autoimmune encephalitis in young women with acute-onset psychosis.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required tools, 3 red herrings, subtype=P; definite diagnosis rests on the CSF anti-GluN1 assay because CSF cells and MRI are normal and only two of the six symptom groups are present
metadata.revision_reason: October 2026 review round (plan NMDAR-ENC): reachable criteria, pathway order, CSF antibody result in the CSF report, labs rebuilt, characteristic teratoma on ultrasound, case-specific musts, differential and evidence

patient.history_present_illness: This 22-year-old right-handed woman was brought to the emergency department by her mother and roommate after one week of progressively bizarre behavior. According to the roommate, the patient was entirely well and performing normally in her classes until approximately ten days ago, when she developed what appeared to be a mild cold with rhinorrhea and mild sore throat lasting two to three days. She did not seek medical attention for this and seemed to recover fully. Approximately seven days prior to presentation, the roommate noticed the patient had difficulty sleeping, staying up most of the night pacing in their shared room. Over the following days the patient became increasingly withdrawn, missed several classes, which was highly uncharacteristic, and began expressing paranoid ideations, telling her roommate that her professors were 'conspiring against her' and that her phone was being monitored. She stopped eating regularly and became irritable when questioned about her behavior. The roommate initially attributed this to stress from her recent breakup and midterm examinations. Four days prior to presentation, the patient's mother called to check in and was alarmed by her daughter's disorganized speech and flat affect, which the mother described as 'not sounding like herself at all.' The mother drove from out of state and found her daughter's dorm room in disarray. The patient was wearing the same clothes she had been wearing days prior, had not showered, and was sitting on her bed staring at the wall. When her mother attempted to engage her, the patient alternated between flat unresponsiveness and agitated outbursts in which she accused her mother of being an imposter. The mother took the patient to an urgent care clinic two days prior to this presentation, where the patient was evaluated and referred to psychiatry with a preliminary diagnosis of acute psychotic episode, possibly related to her anxiety disorder. A prescription for risperidone 1 mg was provided but the patient refused to take it. Over the subsequent 48 hours her condition did not improve. The mother reports that last night the patient was found standing in the dormitory hallway at 3 AM talking to no one, and today the patient did not recognize her own roommate for several minutes before abruptly returning to baseline. No witnessed seizures, no head trauma, no recent travel, no tick bites, and no known illicit drug use. The patient herself provides a vague and inconsistent history, stating she feels fine but cannot explain her behavior.

neurological_exam.additional: During the 45-minute encounter the patient had two brief episodes (each lasting approximately 5-8 seconds) of staring with behavioral arrest, during which she appeared to lose awareness, followed by immediate return to baseline without post-ictal confusion. These episodes were subtle and initially attributed to inattention. No tongue biting, incontinence, or tonic-clonic activity observed. The patient denied awareness of these episodes.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing intact bilaterally without dysmetria. Rapid alternating movements normal.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light, 3 mm bilaterally. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Facial sensation intact bilaterally. Face symmetric at rest and with activation. Hearing intact to finger rub bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline without fasciculations. No orofacial dyskinesias observed during examination.
neurological_exam.gait: Steady, narrow-based gait. Tandem gait intact. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person and place but hesitates when asked the date, ultimately providing the correct month but incorrect day. Affect is flat with intermittent periods of inappropriate suspiciousness, glancing toward corners of the room and whispering that 'they can hear us.' Speech is fluent with normal rate and rhythm, no paraphasic errors, no word-finding difficulty on confrontation naming. Able to follow two-step commands but occasionally loses track mid-task. Registered 3 out of 3 words but recalled only 1 of 3 at five minutes. Clock drawing mildly disorganized with unevenly spaced numbers and misplaced hands. Montreal Cognitive Assessment score estimated at 23/30 with deficits in delayed recall, attention (serial 7s), and visuospatial domains.
neurological_exam.motor: Tone normal in all four extremities. Strength 5/5 throughout in bilateral upper and lower extremities. No pronator drift. No involuntary movements noted during the examination.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, triceps 2+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 2+ bilaterally, patellar 2+ bilaterally, Achilles 2+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No clonus.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, temperature, vibration, and proprioception in all four extremities. No extinction to double simultaneous stimulation.
